item.title: Presidential Message on the Anniversary of Winning World War II
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Anniversary of Winning World War IIThe White HouseAugust 14, 2026

Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Anniversary of Winning World War IIThe White HouseAugust 14, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseAugust 14, 2026
Today, our Nation celebrates the 81st anniversary of Imperial Japan’s unconditional surrender—the moment American might brought the Second World War to its end in complete and total victory. On this monumental occasion, we pay tribute to the grit and sacrifice of the warriors who defended our homeland and carried the hopes of the free world upon their shoulders.
The road to our victory began in fire at Pearl Harbor, where Imperial Japan’s infamous attack summoned a peaceful Nation to arms. Meeting that assault head-on, the warfighters of the Greatest Generation crossed thousands of miles of open sea, turned the tide of the conflict at Midway, broke the enemy fleet at Leyte Gulf, and seized the fortress islands of Iwo Jima and Okinawa. Each of those battles was waged against a fierce and unyielding enemy that tested the strength of American resolve like never before. In the end, the unbreakable will of America’s Armed Forces drove an empire of conquest to its knees, freed millions from its brutal occupation, and left the American Flag flying over a Pacific restored to freedom.
For 4 long years, the American People bore hardship and loss on a scale this country has never known, and they never once wavered. More than 16 million Americans answered the call to serve, and more than 400,000 of them never came home, laying down their lives on distant shores to keep our Nation free. Through their sacrifice, uncommon courage, and selfless devotion to freedom, America emerged from the deadliest war in history stronger, safer, and immortalized as a symbol of freedom, hope, and liberty in every corner of the world. Eighty-one years later, the peace those warriorswon endures, and a free and democratic Japan stands beside the United States of America as one of our closest allies—our two countries joined by common purpose in the defense of a free and open Indo-Pacific and the pursuit of prosperity for both our peoples.
When Imperial Japan laid down its arms on this day in 1945, America stood victorious over the forces of tyranny, proving to every generation that freedom survives only when brave citizens stand ready to defend it. We owe our deepest gratitude to the Americans who gave their lives in that struggle, the soldiers who charged across open sand into enemy fire, the Marines who stormed beaches, the sailors who stood their posts on burning decks, and the airmen who took flight into the skies above the Pacific. To every one of them, our Nation makes this promise: Their valor will forever live on in the American story, the liberty they won will grow stronger in the hands of all who follow,and the Republic they saved will stand as the mightiest force for good the world has ever known. Together, we salute the Greatest Generation, and we carry their indominable spirit into our own time—proud, vigilant, and free. May God bless the heroes of the Second World War, and may their triumph light the way for our Nation in the centuries to come.

The White HouseAugust 17, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump facilitated the reunification of another child with her family on Monday, August 17, 2026, after being separated during the Ukraine – Russia Federation conflict.
“There is nothing more powerful than reuniting a mother with her child after an extended period of time. My representative and I are focused on helping facilitate the next reunification of individuals who have been separated from their loved ones because of the war between Ukraine and Russia,” asserted First Lady Melania Trump.
To date, First Lady Melania Trump’s efforts have facilitated the reunification of 34 children and families since she penned the Peace Letter to Russia’s President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Presidential Message on National Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve Week
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve WeekThe White HouseAugust 17, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseAugust 17, 2026
The citizen warriors of the National Guard and Reserve carry forward a tradition as old as our Republic itself, building careers in the communities they serve while answering our Nation’s call in its hour of need. Their service strengthens our communities, powers our economy, and keeps our military second to none. During National Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve Week, we honor our heroes in uniform and the patriotic employers who stand behind them—a partnership that sustains our all-volunteer force and secures the cause of American freedom.
National Guardsmen and Reservists across our great country are fellow Americans who teach our children, raise our buildings, grow our food, care for our sick, and strengthen our economy. When their country summons them, they answer without hesitation by deploying overseas as part of our Armed Forces or responding here at home to hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and other crises with fearless resolve.
Since returning to office, I have directed the National Guard to restore law and order, secure our borders, and protect our communities. I have mobilized National Guardsmen to some of America’s most dangerous cities, where they stand constant vigil over transit hubs, public spaces, and federal facilities, freeing local authorities to pursue the violent criminals who have terrorized law-abiding citizens for too long. Thanks to their efforts, in 2025 violent crime fell at a pace unmatched in modern American history, the property crime dropped by over 12% from the year before – the second largest in history, and our Nation is on track for its lowest homicide rate in more than a century this year after tying the record in 2025. In the first half of this year alone, murders across our major cities are falling 18 percent, and carjackings are dropping by nearly half. Business owners who once closed their shops at sundown now stay open into the evening, employers can staff late-night shifts they struggled to fill a year ago, and parents can let their children live in their communities without fear of tragedy. In town centers and neighborhoods written off for decades, Americans are opening more businesses, buying more homes, and putting down roots once more, thanks to the heroic actions of our National Guardsmen.
None of the National Guard and Reserve’s tremendous accomplishments would be possible without America’s employers, who keep faith with their workforce wherever duty calls. From family-owned shops on Main Street to the largest corporations in our country, these employers hold positions open, keep benefits in place, and welcome their employees home after every mission. They give National Guardsmen and Reservists the flexibility and support they need to train, deploy, and fulfill their military duties without sacrificing the careers they have worked hard to build. In return, they gain some of America’s best workers, whose leadership, discipline, and skills are strengthened through their service.
This week, the First Lady and I salute every National Guardsman and Reservist, the military spouses and families whose sacrifice at home makes every mission possible, and the employers who stand behind them. Together, we will keep our communities thriving and our Armed Forces the strongest and most respected the world has ever known.

item.title: $2 Million Donation Expands First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Initiative to Indiana University and Purdue University

The White HouseAugust 20, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future initiative will expand its national network through a $2 million donation from IndyCar and Fox Corporation to fund scholarships at Indiana University and Purdue University.
First Lady Melania Trump drew attention to America’s next generation during today’s Rose Garden ceremony: “America’s greatest competitive advantage remains in its own people. Tomorrow’s leaders are sitting in classrooms today, including those growing up in foster care. Their capability is no less remarkable.”
“At FOX, we believe in the transformative power of sports to lift up communities and create real opportunity, especially through expanded educational access. We are proud to partner with the Fostering the Future initiative to fund scholarships at Indiana University and Purdue University, giving extraordinary students the tools to build bright futures,” said Eric Shanks, CEO and Executive Producer, FOX Sports.
The expansion brings the First Lady’s Fostering the Future network to 26 academic institutions nationwide, joining leading universities such as the Ohio State University, University of Wisconsin, Arizona State University, University of Georgia, University of Texas, Louisiana State University, University of Alabama, and University of Florida to create new pathways to higher education for individuals from the foster care community.
Today’s accomplishment will be prominently featured during the historic Freedom 250 Grand Prix race weekend in Washington, DC, August 22-23, which will be airing on FOX and FOX One. An IndyCar race car featuring BE BEST and Fostering the Future branding was displayed in the White House Rose Garden during the announcement and will carry the partnership’s message into race weekend.
This innovative marketing initiative also aims to raise awareness and support for America’s foster care community. Every race car in the Freedom 250 Grand Prix will feature a specially designed BE BEST logo, ensuring that the winner crosses the finish line in support of this vital initiative. Sunday’s Race Day will feature the stars of IndyCar racing on a first-of-its-kind course wrapping around the National Mall with breathtaking views of several iconic landmarks and the Fostering the Future logo prominently displayed on the track on the overpass at 7th Street and Jefferson Drive.
“The First Lady is an incredible champion for students across the county, and this initiative is critical to unlocking a more promising future for so many bright young minds,” said IndyCar President J. Douglas Boles.
First Lady Melania Trump proclaimed, “Fostering the Future elevates America’s youth based on merit and talent, lifting them beyond economic circumstance and every other condition that may limit opportunity.”
The First Lady’s remarks, as prepared for delivery, are below.
A Transformative, Merit Based Initiative
Welcome to the White House.
A warm welcome to our distinguished guests today — Mr. President; my father, Mr. Knavs; Cabinet Members; Mr. Penske; Mr. Boles; Mr. Shanks; the talented drivers; our universities; and the remarkable individuals who stand in support of my Fostering the Future initiative.
The greatest investment America can make is not in technology, infrastructure, or capital markets — it’s our children.
We are at the beginning of an era defined by artificial intelligence, robotics, and industries that have yet to be imagined. But America’s greatest competitive advantage remains in its own people.
Tomorrow’s leaders are sitting in classrooms today, including those growing up in foster care. Their capability is no less remarkable.
Fostering the Future elevates America’s youth based on merit and talent, lifting them beyond economic circumstance and every other condition that may limit opportunity.
Our mission is simple yet transformational: provide every young person from the foster care community the chance to earn a college education, launch a meaningful career, and achieve lasting financial independence.
Today, Indiana University and Purdue University join Fostering the Future’s growing coast-to-coast alliance of leading academic institutions. Congratulations and thank you! Together, they expand a national network of 26 universities that prepare our foster youth to shape America’s growth.

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseAugust 24, 2026
America’s vast and wondrous national parks stand at the heart of our story, preserving the lands our ancestors cherished and the unmatched splendor of a continent like no other. During National Park Week, we celebrate the rich cultural heritage, grandeur, and exceptionalism found in the more than 400 national parks and monuments across our land.
On August 25, 1916, the National Park Service was established to protect our Nation’s natural resources, historic landmarks, and magnificent landscapes. For more than a century, our treasured parks, battlefields, and monuments have stood as hallmarks of the American Spirit, drawing enthusiasts from all walks of life to seek out places of historical significance along with some of the world’s most incredible natural wonders—from coastal landscapes, pristine glacial lakes, and rugged forests to rushing waterfalls, hiking trails, and wild game found nowhere else on Earth.
My Administration is committed to protecting every acre of our lands and preserving the cleanest air and water in the world. During my first term, I was proud to sign the Great American Outdoors Act—the most significant conservation policy since President Teddy Roosevelt—to address prior mismanagement, maintenance backlogs, and critical infrastructure needs in our national parks and public lands. Upon returning to office, I signed the Make America Beautiful Again Executive Order, establishing a commission devoted to promoting voluntary stewardship of our lands, expanding outdoor access, cutting needless regulations, and recovering imperiled species all while growing our economy and protecting the time-honored integrity of our national parks. In response, the Commission issued its Make America Beautiful Again report, calling on the American people, private businesses, and non-profit groups to partner with the federal government and each other to ensure that the next 250 years of our great nation are beautiful, successful, and secure. To mark this milestone year for the National Park Service, I am pleased to announce that on August 25 our national parks will be open free of charge to residents of the United States, giving families the opportunity to see firsthand the natural beauty of our magnificent Republic. Under my leadership, we will make America’s Great Outdoors a source of national pride and breathtaking splendor once again, vowing always to defend our God-given heritage through responsible conservation and bold restoration efforts.
As our Nation commemorates 250 glorious years of Independence, we give thanks for the abundant natural resources of our homeland and for the generations of Americans whose labor preserved these treasures. Together, we will ensure that our majestic national parks endure as a source of adventure, respite, inspiration, and awe for generations to come.

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseAugust 24, 2026
During Overdose and Drug Poisoning Awareness Week, our Nation renews its resolve to defeat the scourge of illicit drugs and synthetic poisons that have devastated hundreds of thousands of American lives. My Administration is relentlessly confronting this threat at every source, and we will always put our national security and the safety, health, and well-being of the American People first.
When I returned to office, I vowed to stop the flow of fentanyl and other deadly drugs into our country, and my Administration immediately took action. We created the Homeland Security Task Force to bring together all federal, state and local partners to achieve the national policy goal of eliminating the cartel presence in America once and for all. By doing so, my Administration secured our southern border and began dismantling fentanyl supply chains at every link, from the narco-terrorist cartels and gangs that traffic these deadly drugs to the foreign suppliers that enable them. I proudly signed the HALT Fentanyl Act, permanently classifying fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs, ensuring dealers and traffickers will receive the maximum force of the law. I designated fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction and the worst cartels as foreign terrorist organizations, unleashing our national security resources against this attack on American soil. I have also directed military forces to conduct strikes on dozens of narcotrafficking boats to disrupt the flow of maritime supply routes. As a result, fentanyl deaths dropped 22 percent in a single year, total drug overdose deaths fell 14 percent, and thousands of American lives have been saved.
The strength of our country rests upon the health of its people, and my Administration is restoring hope in every community touched by addiction. Earlier this year, I launched the Great American Recovery Initiative, uniting government, healthcare, faith communities, and the private sector behind one mission of prevention, treatment, and recovery. This program is making proven treatments more accessible, supporting Americans and families on the road to recovery, and giving every person the opportunity to build a healthy and hopeful future.
This week, we remember every American lost to overdose and drug poisoning, stand with the families who carry their memory, and support all those working to overcome addiction. Above all, we vow to end the devastation wrought by deadly drugs and build a stronger, healthier, and safer America.

The White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
During National Recovery Month, we celebrate the more than 23 million Americans who have found a pathway from addiction to recovery, we recognize those who have helped them reclaim their lives, and we renew our commitment to supporting those still struggling to find hope and healing.
Throughout every community in America, the effects of drug and alcohol addiction are felt in the lives of families, friends, and neighbors. Today, 48.4 million Americans suffer from addiction, and 69,973 Americans died last year to overdose. Every American deserves to live free from the grip of addiction—and my Administration is wholly committed to making that possible by preventing drug use before it starts, providing treatment at the earliest opportunity, and helping more Americans lead engaged and productive lives in recovery.
In January, I was proud to establish the Great American Recovery Initiative, coordinating a national response to the disease of addiction across government, healthcare, faith communities, and the private sector while fostering a culture that celebrates recovery. I also signed an Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets to make our communities safer and help homeless Americans access addiction and mental health services needed to rebuild their lives. I am directing the Food and Drug Administration to prioritize non-opioid options for chronic pain, and I signed the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act to strengthen federal grant programs for treatment, overdose response, and mental health care. We are also stopping deadly drugs before they ever reach our shores. I signed the HALT Fentanyl Act into law, classifying all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs; formally designated major international drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations; sealed our border; and empowered our brave Border Patrol and Armed Forces with the resources needed to carry out massive drug seizures to keep fentanyl off our streets.
Recovery is a testament to the strength of the American Spirit and the promise of a second chance. This month, we stand with those on the road to recovery and the families and communities who support them along the way. Together, we will help more Americans break free from addiction and lead healthy, productive, and fulfilling lives.

The White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
This National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, my Administration stands with the countless children facing the devastating effects of cancer. We recognize the love, strength, and care of the families who walk beside them through every step of their journeys. Above all, we commit to advancing lifesaving innovation and accelerating cures, giving every child the chance to live a long, healthy, and happy life.
American medicine has achieved remarkable breakthroughs in the fight to save the lives of our children, but cancer still remains the leading cause of death among children in the United States. To overcome such devastation, my Administration is strengthening preventative efforts, developing better treatments, and ultimately finding a cure to end this scourge.
Through the Make America Healthy Again Commission, we are addressing the root cause of chronic illnesses afflicting children—including cancer—and giving every child the chance to grow up healthy. We are also harnessing Artificial Intelligence to accelerate pediatric cancer research, identify promising solutions, and unlock new possibilities for prevention and cures. By bringing together American innovation and cutting-edge technology, we are providing new hope to children and families fighting cancer.
Every American child deserves the chance to grow up healthy and achieve their own unique American Dream. Together, we will fight to eradicate this vicious disease and build a future of greater hope, health, and possibility for America’s children.

item.title: Presidential Message on National Preparedness Month
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Preparedness MonthThe White HouseSeptember 2, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
America has always been a nation of strong, capable, and determined people who understand that strength must be built before crisis. Preparedness builds that strength, and readiness is the result. This National Preparedness Month, I call on every American citizen to ready themselves and their families, homes, businesses, and communities for natural and man-made threats.
Readiness begins with understanding the risks that matter most. Before a crisis, Americans can take practical steps to protect their homes and property, purchase affordable insurance against the risks they face, know evacuation routes, maintain an emergency kit with essential supplies, and stay informed through trusted local news and real-time alerts. These simple investments save lives, protect livelihoods, and help families and communities return to normal.
The same principle applies to the systems that power our Nation. American businesses and operators of critical infrastructure have an essential role and must also be ready. The energy, communications, transportation, financial, water, food, and health systems that power American life must remain available when we need them most. My Administration is working to strengthen the reliability of these systems, secure vital supply chains, reduce dangerous dependencies, and ensure services continue operating through crisis.
On June 23, 2026, I issued the National Resilience Strategy that articulates how the Nation, through federalism, will achieve a readiness posture. As President, my Administration continues transforming emergency management in the United States around readiness, responsibility, and results. States and communities must participate in this transformation by building their own fiscal and operational capacity to manage the emergencies they routinely face and support one another through mutual aid, drastically speeding up deployment and delivery of critical resources when disaster strikes. Americans deserve state and local governments that respond quickly to their needs, enabling communities to rebuild stronger and more resilient than ever before. This allows the Federal Government to concentrate its resources on the greatest risks and catastrophic incidents—regionally or nationally. It also makes our country harder to threaten. When America functions through crisis, our adversaries have fewer opportunities to harm us and fewer opportunities to achieve their objectives.
Strength begins with a Nation that is ready to act and such readiness is embodied by Americans who stand strong, who never back down, and who always put America First. This month, we honor our brave first responders, law enforcement officers, emergency personnel, and selfless volunteers. When the alarm sounds, they do not hesitate. They answer the call, protect their fellow Americans, and help keep our communities and our Nation safe and secure. Together, we resolve to build a more prepared, ready, and resilient America.

On Wednesday, September 2, 2026, the President signed into law:
H.R. 6500, the “Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027,” which includes a short-term continuing resolution that provides fiscal year 2027 appropriations to Federal agencies through December 11, 2026, for continuing projects and activities of the Federal Government, and extends authorities for a broad range of programs including surface transportation and veteran programs.
